arxiv-2105-14772.title: Energy-Efficient and Federated Meta-Learning via Projected Stochastic Gradient Ascent
arxiv-2105-14772.creator: Anis Elgabli, Chaouki Ben Issaid, Amrit S. Bedi † , Mehdi Bennis, Vaneet Aggarwal ∗
arxiv-2105-14772.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose an energy-efficient federated meta-learning framework. The objective is to enable learning a meta-model that can be fine-tuned to a new task with a few number of samples in a distributed setting and at low computation and communication energy consumption.

arxiv-2112-01965.title: Theoretical rheo-physics of silk: Intermolecular associations reduce the critical specific work for flow-induced crystallisation
arxiv-2112-01965.creator: Charley Schaefer, Tom C. B. McLeish
arxiv-2112-01965.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Charley Schaefer, Tom C. B. McLeish. Silk is a semi-dilute solution of randomly coiled associating polypeptide chains that crystallise following the stretch-induced disruption, in the strong extensional flow of extrusion, of the solvation shell around their amino acids. We propose that natural silk spinning exploits both the exponentially-broad stretch-distribution generated by associating polymers in extensional flow and the criterion of a critical concentration of sufficiently-stretched chains to nucleate flow-induced crystallisation.

arxiv-2203-00390.title: Mitigating the Hubbard Sign Problem with Complex-Valued Neural Networks
arxiv-2203-00390.creator: Marcel Rodekamp, Evan Berkowitz, Christoph Gäntgen, Stefan Krieg, Thomas Luu, Johann Ostmeyer
arxiv-2203-00390.description: Abstract Monte Carlo simulations away from half-filling suffer from a sign problem that can be reduced by deforming the contour of integration. Such a transformation, which induces a Jacobian determinant in the Boltzmann weight, can be implemented using neural networks. This additional determinant cost for a generic neural network scales cubically with the volume, preventing large-scale simulations.

arxiv-2204-01530.title: Degenerated Noisy Matrix Completion
arxiv-2204-01530.creator: Jafar Jafarov
arxiv-2204-01530.description: Abstract Exact matrix completion and low rank matrix estimation problems has been studied in different underlying conditions. In this work we study exact low-rank completion under non-degenerate noise model. Non-degenerate random noise model has been previously studied by many researchers under given condition that the noise is sparse and existing in some of the columns.

arxiv-2409-10997.title: Contextual Breach: Assessing the Robustness of Transformer-based QA Models
arxiv-2409-10997.creator: Asir Saadat, Nahian Ibn Asad, Md Farhan Ishmam Department of Computer Science and Engineering,Islamic University of Technology {asirsaadat, nahian36, farhanishmam}@iut-dhaka.edu
arxiv-2409-10997.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Asir Saadat, Nahian Ibn Asad, Md Farhan Ishmam Department of Computer Science and Engineering,Islamic University of Technology {asirsaadat, nahian36, farhanishmam}@iut-dhaka.edu. Contextual question-answering models are susceptible to adversarial perturbations to input context, commonly observed in real-world scenarios. These adversarial noises are designed to degrade the performance of the model by distorting the textual input. We introduce a unique dataset that incorporates seven distinct types of adversarial noise into the context, each applied at five different intensity levels on the SQuAD dataset.

arxiv-2412-10030.creator: Francesco Benetti 1,2,3 , Andrea Lapi 1,2,3,4 , Samuele Silveravalle 1,2,3 , Stefano Liberati 1,2,3 , Balakrishna S. Haridasu 1,2,3 , Yacer Boumechta 1,2,3,5 , Minahil Adil Butt 1,2,3 , Carlo Baccigalupi 1,2,3,6

arxiv-2503-03921.title: CREStE : Scalable Mapless Navigation with Internet Scale Priors and Counterfactual Guidance
arxiv-2503-03921.creator: Arthur Zhang, Harshit Sikchi, Amy Zhang, Joydeep Biswas
arxiv-2503-03921.description: Abstract We introduce CREStE , a scalable learning-based mapless navigation framework to address the open-world generalization and robustness challenges of outdoor urban navigation. Key to achieving this is learning perceptual representations that generalize to open-set factors (e.g. novel semantic classes, terrains, dynamic entities) and inferring expert-aligned navigation costs from limited demonstrations.

arxiv-2503-14330.title: Self-Similarity of Loop Amplitudes
arxiv-2503-14330.creator: Kang-Sin Choi
arxiv-2503-14330.description: Abstract We present an amplitude-generating formula in renormalizable quantum field theory. It reflects the self-similarity of loop amplitudes, in which an amplitude can also be a subamplitude of another. Amplitudes are generated by a small number of “irreducible” ones, which may replace tree-level couplings to form more complex amplitudes. Quantum Field Theory provides a successful framework for describing fundamental interactions.

arxiv-2508-00156.title: Integrating Opinion Dynamics into Safety Control for Decentralized Airplane Encounter Resolution
arxiv-2508-00156.creator: Shuhao Qi, Zhiqi Tang, Zhiyong Sun, Sofie Haesaert
arxiv-2508-00156.description: Abstract As the airspace becomes increasingly congested, decentralized conflict resolution methods for airplane encounters have become essential. While decentralized safety controllers can prevent dangerous midair collisions, they do not always ensure prompt conflict resolution. As a result, airplane progress may be blocked for extended periods in certain situations.

arxiv-2508-07742.title: A Rule-Based Approach to Specifying Preferences over Conflicting Facts and Querying Inconsistent Knowledge Bases
arxiv-2508-07742.creator: Meghyn Bienvenu, Camille Bourgaux, Katsumi Inoue, Robin Jean
arxiv-2508-07742.description: Abstract Repair-based semantics have been extensively studied as a means of obtaining meaningful answers to queries posed over inconsistent knowledge bases (KBs). While several works have considered how to exploit a priority relation between facts to select optimal repairs, the question of how to specify such preferences remains largely unaddressed.

pmc-10614330.description: BackgroundMonoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting the Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide (CGRP) pathway are safe and effective treatments for migraine prevention. pmc-11375760.title: Gastric cancer and brain metastasis: A systematic review and meta‑analysis
pmc-11375760.creator: George Fotakopoulos, Grigorios Christodoulidis, Vasiliki Epameinondas Georgakopoulou, Nikolaos Trakas, Pagona Skapani, Konstantinos Panagiotopoulos, Demetrios A. Spandidos, Nicolas Foroglou
pmc-11375760.description: Gastric cancer (GC) constitutes one of the most wide-ranging cancers, with brain metastasis (BM) being a markedly uncommon and unfavorable outcome. The present meta-analysis evaluated the relationship between no-surgical treatment vs. additional surgical BM resection on the patient's quality of life and potential survival using electronic databases, including PubMed (1980-April 2024), Medline (1980-April 2024), Cochrane Library, and EMBASE (1980-April 2024).

pmc-12835447.description: PurposeChildbirth-related fears contribute to both physical and psychological challenges in women, including complicated deliveries and postpartum depression.
